docs.title: How Much Does Silence Help? A Replication and Extension of Brennholt and Vanstone (2014)
docs.description: A widely cited study by Brennholt and Vanstone (2014) found that students who studied in silence recalled more than students who studied with background music. We report a direct replication of their first study, extended with a white-noise group and a group that chose its own music. Recall showed some trends favoring silence, but recall did not consistently differ between any groups. Differences shrank further after students had a second chance to study the passage. A meta-analysis of all direct replications showed small advantages for silence that were not statistically significant. Choosing one study condition for every student is premature.
